The key sits on the desk leather. Brass. Small teeth. No inn tag. Lamp oil, river water, and a quiet that isn't empty.
File the night. The key stays put. I have closed a case on less — and been wrong in a way ink doesn't show.
Work the morning. If the gray greatcoat comes for the key, he can take a number. I am done calling coats an ending.
Come in out of the wet. Tell me what the city already knows.
Sit down. Two nights past: last place, last word, last soul who saw her.
Convince me she didn't buy a room and a new name.
My sister Lillian vanished two nights past. Not left. Not fled. The lamps were still lit. The kettle still held heat. The apartment's hush-ward hadn't tripped.
Mr. Voss? Forgive the hour. They told me the night clerk only takes living errands after dawn.
strings.dlg.empty-coat.intro.node.lila.key.revea: Since I found it, a man has been following me. Gray greatcoat. Black gloves. He waits across from my boarding house and turns away when I look. He doesn't wave. The streetlamps dim a fraction when he stands under them.

Sewn into the lining: a brass key. Small. Old teeth. No inn tag. It hummed once against my palm and went quiet. Lillian still sews her own hems. She would not leave a coat that cost her a week — or a key that cost her more.
strings.dlg.empty-coat.intro.node.lila.plea.b.te: If the gray greatcoat comes looking for the key, don't give it to him. I hired you to find my sister. Not to finish someone else's ritual.
strings.dlg.empty-coat.intro.node.lila.plea.text: Please find her, Mr. Voss. Find the sister — not the coat's alibi.
strings.dlg.empty-coat.intro.node.lila.police.st: I asked for the night sergeant's notes. He offered coffee and a speech about tides and "what the river keeps." I asked who benefited if Lillian stopped reading manifests. He stopped offering coffee.

Harborpoint Watch filed it soft: missing adult, no struggle, coat recovered, probable drowning. Case cooling before the ink dried. They were polite. They did not offer the file — or the reading-rights on it.
strings.dlg.empty-coat.intro.node.lila.reply.cyn: Lillian hated the river. She hated an unfinished book more. The watch found her coat and called it an ending. I put my hands in the lining.
If she had a clean alibi I would not be dripping on your floor.
Fine. Mark your coin. Look at the coat first. Whoever emptied it left the key — and meant you to.
At least you're honest about the bill.
I'll take the key. I'll take the case. Don't wait on a raven — or the hush-charm on the sill.
You'll take it. That's enough. You get the key.
strings.dlg.empty-coat.intro.node.lila.reply.goo: She worked late at the shipping office near Wharf Ladder — ledgers, manifests, seals that bite if you read them wrong. Never missed the morning ferry. Two nights past she left at nine. By midnight the river had her coat.
Thank you. Two hundred now — good coin, not dock-ledger chalk. The rest when you find her.
The pockets were turned inside out — careful work, not panic.
I'll take the key. I'll take the case. Don't wait on a raven — or the hush-charm on the sill.
The follower: tall, hat brim low, gloves that stay on. He never crosses the street. He only makes sure I know it's his.
I'll take the promise. I'll walk carefully.
strings.dlg.empty-coat.intro.node.lila.reply.neu: Last confirmed: Wharf Ladder shipping office, two nights past, nine. She told a clerk she had one more errand uptown. No name. No hired coach chalked on the desk slate. Midnight, river watch found her coat on the stones below the old iron stairs — empty. Arranged. Like an offering someone wanted found.
They handed the coat back in a paper bag. I took it home and found the key they never felt for.
That's the work I came to buy — river stones, duty roster, the shipping-office clock that runs three minutes fast when the night crew wants an alibi the wards will swear to.
I'll take the key. I'll take the case. Don't wait on a raven — or the hush-charm on the sill.
I'll stay with a friend on Printers' Quarter tonight. Real locks. A threshold that holds. Fewer witnesses who owe the docks a favor.

Gray greatcoat, black gloves, no limp, no badge. Bakery doorway across from my stairs, eleven to one. When a cart rattles past, he uses the noise to move. Professional habits — or something wearing them.
strings.dlg.empty-coat.intro.node.lila.reply.pre: I'll take the key. I'll take the case. Don't wait on a raven — or the hush-charm on the sill.
Fine. Lillian was reading manifests. I don't have the names clean enough for a magistrate's hall. I have a sister and a key.
strings.dlg.empty-coat.intro.node.lila.triad.key: Describe the follower once more, then go somewhere with a real lock — and a threshold that holds.
If anyone asks, I never saw a key.
Tell me what you're still not saying. What did Lillian find in those manifests?

I'm leaving the key if you'll take the case. Two hundred now. The rest when you find her.

Tell me how you want to play this.
strings.dlg.empty-coat.intro.node.lila.triad.pol: I pull the file they won't show you.
The drowning's too tidy. I'll hear how they blessed it.
I'll tell the sergeant I believe him. See who relaxes.
The watch have a coat. I have a sister. What do you do with that?
strings.dlg.empty-coat.intro.node.voss.monologue: Rain had been working the glass since afternoon. The ward on the sill hadn't bothered to argue.
Three unpaid notices. Same name on every one. Coin that never quite warmed in the hand.
Hearth ticks. Pipes talking in the walls. Rain on the glass. Same as yesterday — and the night I trusted a tide chart more than a sister.

I told myself I was done with missing persons. The rent — and whatever listens for rent in this building — said otherwise.

Then the hallway. Heels on tired boards. A pause outside the door, like someone testing a threshold. Like someone who had already been told the river was answer enough.

A woman out of the rain. A coat that remembered a body and had forgotten the rest.

The door opened. I already hated how familiar that shape felt.
The key sits on the desk leather. Brass. Small teeth. No inn tag. Lamp oil, river water, and a quiet that isn't empty.
Three cold cases, two debts the ledger still remembers, one page that hasn't learned a name yet.
The hall smelled worse — damp wool, old wards, someone else's business. At least it led somewhere.
strings.dlg.inspect.office.files.node.inspection: Sealed. Abandoned. And one folio I still lied about — to the client, and to whatever keeps the cabinet shut.
strings.dlg.inspect.office.phone.node.inspection: Empty iron perch. Droppings on the desk-leather edge. For once the bird had the decency to stay gone — and look guilty doing it.
strings.dlg.inspect.office.window.node.inspectio: Same rain, same glass. Now I had a client — and a key that hummed when the weather turned.
The rain had been working the glass longer than I had. The sill-ward didn't care either way.
strings.dlg.journal.chrono.client-retained: Retained by Lila March. The Empty Coat is open.
strings.dlg.journal.chrono.pressed-hard: Pushed Lila on what the watch finished too early. Manifests.
